#4861. 15 Best Bedroom Lighting Ideas for a Relaxing Ambience (2026)

When you’re trying to unwind at the end of a long day, turning on the “big light” is simply not the move. The glare of a way-too-bright overhead light is not only unflattering but oftentimes overstimulating. It can make your otherwise cozy bedroom feel more like a department-store dressing room, leaving relaxation a little bit harder to come by. The right bedroom lighting, on the other hand, can bring a sense of warmth, atmosphere, and visual interest to the space where you spend some of your most cherished downtime.

The secret lies in layered lighting, which involves a series of soft illumination sources working together in concert: A bedside lamp provides focused task lighting for reading, while wall sconces free up valuable nightstand space and introduce a soft diffused glow. Floor lamps can brighten an otherwise neglected corner, and a beautiful chandelier or pendant light doubles as a bedroom’s focal point, even when the light is switched off.

Dimmable fixtures and warm white light bulbs can be especially transformational in bedrooms that also function as an office or a hangout space. Ahead, we’ve rounded up our favorite bedroom lighting ideas, including sculptural statement pieces, portable table lamps, and wall-mounted fixtures that usher in a sense of calm.

For a reading nook, a work-from-home space, or just a little warm white lighting, a floor lamp can show off your taste without sacrificing functionality. We’ve pulled two designer-favorite must-haves for those in the world of interior design.

This 1960s model from Danish designer Mads Caprani hasn’t gone out of style since its release. The pleated shade, bentwood spine, and U-shaped cast-iron base make it one of the most easily recognized and iconic designs in floor lamps to this day. If you’re looking to make a statement about your style, this piece does just that—landing somewhere between studious and stylish, as in polo champion Nacho Figueras’s Florida home.

Another lamp for tastemakers, this design from Isamu Noguchi has made the rounds in many celebrity home tours from a minimalist Brooklyn brownstone to Troye Sivan’s modern Melbourne home. Commerce director Rachel Fletcher has previously named a Noguchi lamp one of her bedroom essentials. The reputation of Noguchi’s work and the unique style of his Akari lamps make this a design staple for anyone hoping to cultivate a modern bedroom.

We love the look of dual table lamps to frame your bed and create a distinct visual space in your bedroom. It also allows your bed to feel like a conscious design choice instead of a strictly functional piece. We’re taking bedside lamp notes from this Portland home owned by the lead singer of The Shins and decorated by Jessica Helgerson. And, if you don’t want to do things matchy-matchy, any one of these lamps would look great solo too.

We love this moody metallic option from Article for a midcentury look—and we named it one of our favorite bedside lamps after ample editor testing. At $149, the price is also right.

If you’re struggling to find a table lamp that plays well with others, this is a viable option from coastal core experts Serena & Lily. This comes in four beautiful shades, inspired by the Italian shoreline, and there’s even a touch of rattan for a beachy bedside table moment.

The Flos Bellhop table lamp is a great source of ambient light in this minimalist Barcelona bedroom.

A godsend for a bedroom with inconvenient outlets, these design-forward portable lamps bring both ambience and task lighting wherever you need them.

Another favorite of interior designers, the Flos Bellhop table lamp is a great source of ambient light in a minimalist setting. These super-portable LED lamps have four dimmer settings, are USB-compatible, and can last up to 24 hours on a single charge. And, if you love the simple glass shape, they’re also available as wall sconces for a stylish outdoor lighting moment.

You never know when you’ll need a little extra light, and the Poldina Pro can adapt to your ever-changing needs. The lamp pairs a petite silhouette with the clean lines of Italian minimalist design, making it a versatile fit for your nightstand, dresser, or reading nook. Without any unsightly wires to speak of, the lamp can appear as an intentional design choice just about anywhere. Its touch-sensitive dimmer lets you adjust the brightness and choose between three color temperatures.

AD shopping writer Julia Harrison, who tested the Micro version, appreciates its versatility for desk work and kitchen prep alike. She notes that the lamp “blends shyly and seamlessly into all setups that require a little, but not too much, light.” With approximately 12 hours of battery life, it’s an especially convenient option for adding a little extra illumination wherever you need it.

Wall lighting brings a warm dimension to the design of your bedroom and provides great task lighting for a bedtime read. While we love table lamps on matching nightstands, wall sconces bring an added degree of intentionality in their design, as seen in Walton Goggins’s guest bedroom and Jennifer Garner’s kid’s bedroom.

Available in 24 colors and with flexible orientation, this wall sconce channels the fun throwback design sensibility of Portland-based Schoolhouse. Not relegated to the bedroom alone, these fixtures can bring vibrancy to any space—as is evident in the bathroom of this timeless, edgy Massachusetts home.

A visible mending detail modernizes a traditional style, so the pleated lampshade remains classic without being too precious. We love to imagine this lining a long entryway, or on either side of a tall headboard—the perfect lighting for bedtime pages.

Linen shades are classic for a reason: They soften the appearance of a light fixture, giving even the most straightforward silhouettes a dash of warmth and character. Quince’s Contemporary Sconce pairs crisp white linen shades with a streamlined steel frame, available in brass or black for two distinctly different looks. The brass finish befits a more traditional bedroom, while the black feels especially sharp juxtaposed against pale walls and minimalist decor. Choose a single or double configuration depending on your space, or install a matching pair on either side of the bed for a polished alternative to bedside table lamps.

If a flower could moonlight as a light fixture, it would probably look something like Soho Home’s Florie Wall Light. Inspired by the interiors of White City House, the members’ club in West London, the sculptural design features two gently curved layers of champagne-colored glass that resemble a tulip’s petals. A fluted, bubbled texture gives the glass an almost vintage quality, while the frosted finish diffuses the light into a soft, atmospheric glow. Even at just nine inches tall and nine inches wide, the fixture has enough personality to stand on its own, though opting for a pair to flank the bed would be an especially charming choice to imbue the space with a dash of romance.

Actress Laura Harrier hangs a bespoke pendant lamp in her bedroom.

The wrong kind of flush mount can be an eyesore, and the right kind of pendant light can transform a space from tragic to tasteful. These picks from IKEA and Lumens are both contemporary yet classic, proving them a satisfying finishing touch that makes all the difference.

IKEA brings an affordable yet still-elevated style to the lineup with this ubiquitous, rattan-like pendant (technically latticed bamboo) from Ilse Crawford. We love this style as much for dining room lighting as we do for bedroom lighting. Can’t decide which? Two will only cost you $140 total.

Danish lighting design has a knack for making even the most practical objects feel like works of art. Case in point: the PH 5 Hanging Lamp. Its distinctive arrangement of overlapping shades creates a sculptural silhouette, with each layer directing and diffusing light. The three-shade system sends most of the illumination downward while allowing a softer glow to escape around the sides for ambient lighting. The result is a striking pendant that commands attention, even when it’s not turned on. The light would look especially beautiful suspended above a bedside table in place of a traditional lamp.

Supermodel Elsa Hosk incorporated a pink Tronchi chandelier, made of Murano glass, into her New York City bedroom.

Might some consider a chandelier too much for a bedroom? Yes, someone who needs to live a little. A chandelier brings a sense of occasion to every space it’s in, and your bedroom deserves no less. These picks bring elegance without overkill.

We love how supermodel Elsa Hosk incorporated a pink Tronchi chandelier made of Murano glass into her New York City bedroom, and you can find a similar pick on 1stDibs if you want to sleep in rose-colored bliss.

Often referred to as the “boob light,” this type of flush mount can get a bad rap, but West Elm has figured out how to make them shine. This contemporary ceiling light fixture is simple, aesthetic, and subtle.

Serena & Lily’s Capiz Scalloped Chandelier has the delicate charm of a seaside find, with a little extra glamour courtesy of its antique-gold framing. Each translucent capiz shell is individually hand-set, creating a softly scalloped silhouette that feels like a piece of jewelry for the ceiling. The natural variations in the shells’ shapes and opacity give the fixture a beautiful sense of movement. Light filters through the overlapping layers to cast a warm diffused glow, making it an especially lovely choice for a bedroom where atmosphere matters just as much as illumination.

If you’re looking for guidance when it comes to your bedroom lights, it’s important to keep a variety of factors in mind. Do you do a lot of reading in bed? Maybe table lamps should be your primary focus. Do you have enough fixtures to keep the space illuminated but not too bright? Perhaps a floor lamp or two will provide that glow for you. Are you spending most of your time winding down and heading to sleep? Try a night-light or string lights for ambience! And, of course, you’ll want multiple light sources to get the look (and the vibe) just right. But don’t fret, we’ve combed the AD home tour archives—and shopping lists—for the best bedroom lights around.

#4859. USDT buyers face 22% VAT when Moscow Exchange opens crypto trading

Buyers will pay VAT on top of the trade price in December because Russia’s tax code has no explicit exemption for foreign digital instruments.

Buyers of Tether’s USDt (USDT) stablecoin will pay a 22% value-added tax (VAT) on top of the trade price when Moscow Exchange (MOEX) opens crypto trading on Dec. 1, according to the exchange’s clearinghouse.

The National Clearing Centre (NCC) said it would apply VAT to USDT purchases, sales and swaps through Dec. 31. A buyer purchasing 100,000 rubles worth of USDT would pay an additional 22,000 rubles in VAT.

Unlike Bitcoin (BTC) and Ether (ETH), which Russia classifies as digital currencies, USDT falls under a separate legal category known as foreign digital instruments. Russia’s tax code excludes sales of digital currencies from VAT, but it provides no explicit exemption for foreign digital instruments, according to the NCC.

The NCC said it had asked Russia’s Federal Tax Service and Finance Ministry for guidance. It said it would update market participants if it received clarification or if lawmakers exempted trades conducted before Jan. 1, 2027.

Bank of Russia rules that took effect Nov. 17 allow non-qualified investors to buy Bitcoin, Ether and USDT through intermediaries, with annual purchases capped at 300,000 rubles (about $3,650) per intermediary.

#4858. 7 Golf Club Sets for Beginners That Will Have You Lowering Your Handicap

Sets from Callaway, Stix, and more offer solid, affordable clubs.

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

IF YOU’RE JUST getting into golf, there will be a time in your life when you need to invest in a golf club set. As it’s a lifetime pursuit, it’s best to invest in a decent setup, and if well maintained, it can last you for years to come. While advanced players may want to customize their own golf club sets, there are numerous brands that make complete sets that will have you playing from day one. Even notable brands like Callaway and Wilson have solid options.

It's true you could go buy pre-owned clubs as your first beginner set, which is not a bad idea to peruse your local Dick's Sporting Goods or local golf shop (especially for previous year model demos during the offseason), brand sites' used portals like Callaway Certified Pre-Owned, or eBay. But if you've gotten the golf bug and are looking for a new-to-you set, these days golf brands are churning out shiny, high-quality sets at affordable entry points. Customization is also better than ever, as several outfitters offer club length adjustments, different club combinations, and a selection of stylish golf bags to accompany them. You can always ask for a set as a great golf gift, too.

Whichever route you choose, we spoke with Paul Silva, head pro at NYC’s Van Cortlandt Golf Club to answer some of the most frequently asked questions when it comes to buying a beginner golf set. After you get a legit set, don't forget about some golf shoes.

When it comes to the game of golf, not many brands can boast expertise in every single category. One that can though is Callaway. The brand behind elite golf balls, top-tier putters, golf bags, pro-worthy irons and drivers, Callaway is no slouch when it comes to making high-quality gear for beginners.

The 2026 XR lineup comes in a 13-piece set, which includes a mallet putter made by Odyssey and its DFX V-line Fang shape, which offers higher stability and more aggressive alignment aids—two elements you’re rarely going to find in an entry-level putter. The irons are classics, based on decades of stellar game-improvement technology, while the hybrids, 3-wood, and driver are modeled after one of golf’s most exciting new weapons of the past couple of years, the Paradym. This year you also get an approach wedge. Add on the fact of its high-MOI V-Line putter and you get a set that dominates the short game. This set will set you back more than most, but don’t be surprised if you tote these clubs along with you for the next ten years.Read More: The Best Golf Shirts

Though technically a slightly older legacy bundle, this platinum set features two premium features we love. The first is the irons. They're well-built and just what you want out of a beginner iron, making them a solid set to build the base of your arsenal for years to come. Considered a game improvement set, they have a thinner top line and are more refined. The second is the golf bag: It's highly comfortable thanks to the dual carrying strap and lightweight design, and comes with ample pocket space.

Wilson is a brand with immense golf pedigree—no player worth their salt will scoff at the brand’s gear, whether you’re shooting even par or 20-over. The set is immensely affordable, so while it will probably long outlast your golf career, it won’t make you feel bad about upgrading once you start to improve.

For someone just getting into the game or hitting the range for the very first time, this set is great to start with. With every club you’ll need to get from the tee box to the green (and probably everywhere in between), this set won’t leave you without an option, no matter how wayward your shots get.

The set has a solid 4.3-out-of-5-star rating on Amazon, with reviewers lauding the set’s value and high level of forgiveness. Odds are high you’ll want to upgrade sooner than later, but if you or someone you know likes to pick up new hobbies, this set will help decide if golf is a lifelong commitment or just a phase.

While one of the most expensive of the bunch, this TaylorMade set is certifiably legit. We're talking about a beast of a driver which features an adjustable driver, allowing you to change the loft and face angle as your swing evolves (something you hardly ever find on a complete set driver), a beautiful set of high-performance irons, and a stylish golf bag that will protect your investment with reassurance.

This is a set for those who are getting serious and playing several times per week. The barrier to entry is higher than the rest of the options on our list, but when you consider the pedigree of a brand like TaylorMade, you’ll find that the long lifespan of the clubs and golf bag make it a set you can grow into and not have to replace for years.

Picking up on the game quicker than you thought? You can skip the early stages and go for a complete set that allows you to learn how to optimize your shot-making skills. The Stix Perform Set is a complete 12-club set that will provide you with all the tools you need, all for under $1,000.

The Perform Set is the brand’s first set with the option for irons with a steel shaft, a boon for mid-high handicap players whose higher swing speeds may be a bit too much for the extra flex of graphite. Clubs that benefit from the flex (the driver, 3 wood, and 4 hybrid) still come standard with graphite, but having the choice when selecting irons is going to greatly increase the amount of time you’ll stick with your Stix.

In my testing, I took the Stix out for a couple dozen rounds, walking and riding in a cart. The set is very manageable size-wise. The bag is light enough for comfortable wear but big enough to stay secure when strapped to the back of a golf cart. They’re some of the most forgiving clubs I've played and are well-built, resulting in improved distance and fewer mishits. My favorite club was the 4 iron hybrid—I've never hit a hybrid so well.

Another set from one of the most prestigious equipment brands in golf, the Cobra Fly XL set is the ideal set for someone who knows they’re going to be consistently hitting the golf course in a golf cart. The cart bag is big, sturdy, and spacious, while the wide range of clubs gives you options in every part of the course.

The Cobra brand is well-recognized, and these striking clubs will fit in with any other sets on the course, ensuring that your skills do the talking, not your equipment. If your skills are lacking, that’s okay, too, because each club in this set is super forgiving thanks to excellent weight distribution and optimized shape, from the driver right down through the putter.

When you’re looking for a little more performance but still trying to stay affordable, PXG is a brand to look to. This Wildcat Bundle is an extremely versatile setup that utilizes premium materials and the same tech found in the brand’s standalone clubs, all tuned for maximum forgiveness and easy launch—must-haves for beginners.

While it is a hefty investment, they’re the one-and-done purchase type, meaning that you won’t outgrow them anytime soon, and will last for years to come. These clubs are meant to bridge the gap from big box store generic clubs and a custom-fitted pro set, while providing a fairway-friendly driver and the brand’s polymer cores for a softer feel and more distance. While it’s only a 9-club set, it has all the essentials you’ll need to make it up and down on any course.

Most beginner sets will include between nine and 11 clubs. 10 is a good sweet spot; it is enough to have a driver, a fairway wood and/or a hybrid, a 5i-9i, a wedge, and a putter. Generally a full set is 14 clubs; that includes the putter—and you can keep no more than that number in your bag during play.

Two recommendations we would make would be to forego a 3-wood in favor of a 5-wood or 4-hybrid—most players don’t actually need a 3-wood and would be better served with a more forgiving hybrid (or two). If you can, consider adding a sand wedge (or potentially a lob wedge that you learn how to use) to sit alongside your pitching wedge, as many pitching wedges aren’t lofted enough for tricky shots in the sand or around the greens.

As Silva told us, "I tell everyone the same thing in the beginning, find a few clubs that you can hit—a hybrid, a 5 iron, a 7 iron, a pitching wedge, a putter. You can learn to do a lot with those things, especially in the beginning. You don’t need to worry so much about distance."

Most beginners will want a shaft made of graphite. These will create greater swing speeds, allowing you to hit the ball further, even as you start to tune your swing. If you’re not a full-on beginner or aren’t looking for any extra distance, a set with steel shafts are a great choice. These will be easier to grow into skill-wise, making it easier to adapt as your game improves. As your swing speed improves, the flex of graphite shafts will be too much, and you’ll need to graduate to iron shafts then.

The main factors in forgiveness are club head and shaft. There’s a lot to dig into with this (we could write an entire essay on these two things), but in general, most beginner sets are outfitted with the absolute easiest club head to hit and a graphite shaft that allows for greater swing speed and fewer mistakes. We’d say not to get caught up in the nitty-gritty and focus on finding a set that is made for new players—something that almost every brand will outline in its product descriptions. Make sure you take a look to see what handicap each club set is designed for and pick the one made for high handicappers (that’s you), as these are coined as player improvement clubs.

Golf club prices run the gamut, but a good set of beginner clubs will usually run you anywhere from $250 to $1,000. This is a huge discrepancy, but there is a big range in quality from bottom to top. If you’re a brand-new golfer, spending $1,000 isn’t necessary, but if you think you’re in it for the long haul and want a set of sticks that are going to allow you to progress without having to upgrade, spending a little more cash is a great idea—the technology really does make a difference and it'll save you with an upgrade in a year or two if you improve.

To help facilitate the best golf club sets on the market in 2026, I consulted with Senior Gear and Commerce Editor Ryan Brower (a mid-handicapper himself) to determine which clubs available are truly worthwhile. We evaluated each on club head size, materials, shaft construction, and forgiveness. Some sets, like the Stix full setup, gave us the chance to see what a quality set of clubs can do for a high handicapper, while the more affordable sets gave us a good idea of what is possible at a low price point. Even for someone like me, who may only get on the links a couple of times a year, using any of the sets listed below can have an instant improvement in gameplay. Brower typically plays around 20 rounds per year, so he definitely knows his way around a course. Ultimately, we picked sets that we liked the most, but there are so many options today, you really can’t go wrong when you’re trying to make a decision, because, hey, you can always upgrade.

Beginners to golf do not need to get a custom fitting for clubs, but if you have the money and want to go all in on your new hobby, then we won't stop you. Really the main measurement you want to get right when buying is proper club sizing (not too tall or too short)—and the good news is most of these clubs will have a solid fit for just starting out.

The only initial adjustments you need to make as a beginner are if you are exceptionally tall or short. If you are over 6'2" consider sizing a half-inch or more length adjustment on your clubs. You can also just opt for a set that has a "Tall" option available. If you are under 5'5", you'll likely want a half-inch decrease in length adjustment.

If you like to go by feel, swinging your friends’ clubs or talking to a pro at your local course will help confirm the sizing you need. As you progress in your game, sizing can be pinpointed down further to personalized club sizing, if you choose.

There's nothing wrong with buying pre-owned clubs to serve as your first beginner set. There is a whole market online for really nice pre-owned clubs for a solid price on sites like Ebay and the golf brands' websites. Yet the downside is, you guessed it, they were somebody else's. There's wear and tear on them.

Instead of buying pre-owned, opt for new. A new set will give you the proper tools to get acclimated on the course and really give you the opportunity to learn the game. Golf is a lot about feel. Your clubs should be your best friend out on the course, not some raggedy set whose best days are long gone.

Buying a new set also gives you something to build off of. As you get better you'll want to make upgrades. Maybe you want a more precise sand wedge or a driver with more power? What you'll do next is swap out single clubs one at a time until you find a set that fits your game to a T.

#4856. How South Korea’s proposed 20% cap could change who runs Upbit

Naver Financial agreed to buy every share in Upbit’s operator, but a proposed ownership cap could strip away its voting rights on four-fifths of them.

When Naver struck its deal for Dunamu, the company behind crypto exchange Upbit, it had already worked out how to retain control of its financial arm.

Agreements with two Dunamu executives would give Naver 46.5% of the votes in Naver Financial despite owning just 17%. Control of Dunamu itself looked simpler, and Naver Financial would own it outright.

However, South Korea’s proposed ownership cap puts that second part of the deal in doubt. If lawmakers approve the bill, shares above the 20% cap would lose their votes.

Related: South Korea to permit crypto withdrawal freezes during hacking threats

With regulatory approval, a shareholder could vote up to 34%. The draft gives regulators no explicit power to order a sale, so Naver Financial could still hold every Dunamu share while losing the vote on most of them. That leaves investors in the $11.2 billion deal with a question the purchase price alone can’t answer.

Who would have the right to appoint the directors who oversee Upbit? The board and contractual rights Naver Financial retains could determine whether its parent can count Dunamu’s earnings in its accounts.

#4855. French Senate Rejects Plan to Make Crypto Holders Declare Self-Custody Wallets

French Senate Rejects Plan to Make Crypto Holders Declare Self-Custody Wallets

France's Senate has rejected a proposal that would have required crypto holders to declare self-custodied wallets worth more than €100,000 ($110,000) to tax authorities, according to the official record of Tuesday's debate on the 2027 budget.

Two identical amendments, one from the Communist-led CRCE-K group and one from a group of senators led by Anne-Sophie Romagny, were voted down after both the government and the Senate's finance committee opposed them. The vote was earlier reported by Cointelegraph.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short BTC with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

The amendments would have obliged holders to declare self-custodied crypto above the threshold. French taxpayers already have to declare crypto accounts held on platforms, but not crypto held in their own wallets.

"The shop window is illuminated, but the back room remains in the dark," CRCE-K senator Alexandre Basquin said, in comments translated from French. The more closely platforms are monitored, the greater the incentive for large holders to keep their crypto themselves, he argued.

Minister for Public Action and Accounts David Amiel said the EU's DAC8 directive, which requires crypto service providers to report users' transactions to tax authorities, had already brought transparency. A purely declarative obligation would not let authorities track how crypto is used in money laundering or tax fraud cases, he said.

The proposal had already passed through France's lower house. The National Assembly's finance committee backed it in October, prompting a backlash from the crypto industry.

The budget was later rejected in the lower house, so the Senate is debating the government's original bill, without the crypto amendments that deputies had added.

On Tuesday, senators also rejected an amendment that would have made swaps from crypto into stablecoins a taxable event. Amiel argued that stablecoins are not money, as they have no legal tender status and are often unstable. A proposal to extend France's exit tax to crypto holdings worth more than €800,000 ($877,000) was also defeated.

Critics of the reporting plan had warned that a register of large crypto holders could become a target in France, which has become the global epicenter of "wrench attacks," in which criminals use violence to force victims to hand over crypto.

France's national anti-organized crime prosecutor's office recorded more than 70 crypto-linked kidnappings and unlawful detentions in the first eight months of 2026, Decrypt reported in September. Authorities charged 88 people, including minors, in a crackdown in April.

Leaks of personal data have added to those fears. A breach of France's tax authority in August exposed records tied to more than 678,000 people and businesses. In January, a tax agent was accused of looking up crypto investors and prison guards in tax databases for an unidentified buyer, Le Parisien reported, while a June attack in Nancy followed a data breach at French crypto tax platform Waltio.

#4853. What Is the Best Type of Yogurt? We Narrowed It Down to the World’s 8 Healthiest.

EVERYBODY LOVE YOGURT. Okay, maybe not everyone, but there's a reason yogurt has been a dietary staple in dozens of countries for centuries. Yogurt doesn't spoil as fast as milk, yet still delivers milk's nutrients—protein, calcium, potassium, magnesium—without the same risk of, um, certain GI issues.

"Most of the world is lactose intolerant and has been for thousands and thousands of years," says Robert Hutkins, PhD, a professor of food microbiology at the University of Nebraska. "Humans figured out that even if they were lactose intolerant, they could still consume cultured milks because the culture helps degrade the lactose before it gets to the colon and gets fermented by gas-producing microbes."

Whether you need help digesting lactose or not, the latest research suggests that yogurt has wide-ranging benefits, from enhancing gut health to improving blood sugar control to maybe even reducing your risk of an early death.

From Europe to Asia to Africa, all yogurt starts with the same basic ingredients: milk and good bacteria. But no two types are exactly alike. Here's what to know before your next grocery run.

Traditional Greek yogurt is strained through a cheesecloth to remove excess fluid. Yogurt factories use centrifuges or special filters instead. What's left behind is a thick, smooth yogurt with a slightly acidic flavor and a concentrated source of nutrients, including about 18 grams of protein per 6-ounce container.

Some food makers add thickeners as a shortcut, so check the label for a simple ingredient list of milk, cream, and yogurt cultures. "The products with thickeners added have a different texture, a little bit more gumminess," says Molly Kimball, RD, CSSD, a dietitian based in Louisiana. Swap in Greek yogurt for sour cream or mayo, or stir it into guacamole—the lactic acid slows down the oxidation that turns avocados brown.

Technically considered a soft cheese, skyr is strained like Greek yogurt to produce something firm yet creamy. It's usually made with skim milk, yielding yogurt with slightly more protein than Greek yogurt: about 19 grams of protein per 6 ounces. Use skyr to make dips hearty enough to stand up to cut vegetables (or chips). Or stir it into bolognese to impart a velvety texture and an extra boost of protein.

This yogurt variety isn't strained, so it has a thinner texture and less protein than its Greek or Icelandic cousins: about 6 grams per 6 ounces. Traditional Bulgarian yogurt gets its signature sharp flavor from high concentrations of the aptly named Lactobacillus Bulgaricus bacteria, which produce lactic acid. Kimball recommends blending Bulgarian yogurt into smoothies to add a tanginess that counterbalances sweeter ingredients.

Most yogurts are fermented in large vats. As yogurt bacteria digest milk, they produce a wide variety of metabolites, including gel-like substances called exopolysaccharides. Then the yogurt is pumped into the smaller containers we snag at the grocery store.

With French-style yogurt, the milk and bacterial cultures are poured into cups earlier, before the microbes multiply. "That gives you a more custardy product because it hasn't gone through this pumping phase that disturbs the gel," says Hutkins. Inside a 6-ounce cup of French-style yogurt, you'll find about 5 grams of protein. To try it the French way, eat your yogurt for dessert, alone or paired with a little honey or jam.

This tangy, thin, pourable yogurt is fermented with kefir grains–gelatinous clusters that contain milk proteins and up to 50 bacterial and yeast species. During fermentation, these yeasts can leave behind traces of alcohol and carbon dioxide, or fizz. However, many mass-produced kefirs use standardized starter cultures instead to maintain consistent product quality and keep the alcohol concentration low enough to sell in grocery stores.

Kimball suggests drinking plain kefir, Russian or otherwise. It packs about 8 grams of protein per cup. If you can't handle the sour flavor, balance it with a teaspoon or less of maple syrup or a few drops of stevia or monk fruit. If you want a flavored variety, pick one with no more than 5 grams of added sugar.

Sweet and mildly acidic, dahi is the key ingredient in Indian staples like lassi–a yogurt drink often flavored with mango, spices, or rosewater–and raita, the sauce that cools your mouth when you order your vindaloo extra hot. Some dahi varieties contain Leuconostoc, bacteria that produce a metabolite called diacetyl that imparts a buttery flavor. Each six-ounce serving of dahi packs about 7 grams of protein.

Drinkable like kefir, laban is sour but smooth and contains about 5 grams of protein per six ounces. Strain it in a colander or cheesecloth to make labneh, a thick, soft, yogurt-like cheese traditionally smeared on sandwiches and stacked on mezze platters.

This drinkable yogurt is often thicker than fermented milk beverages. Its mix of cultures, which hail mostly from the Lactobacillusgenus, imparts a moderately acidic flavor with subtle buttery notes. Amasi packs about 6 grams of protein per six ounces. It's traditionally eaten with maize or sorghum porridge, especially at breakfast.

#4852. Body Recomposition Basics: How to Lose Fat and Gain Muscle, According to a Doctor

Your body recomposition journey starts here.

Body recomposition is the fitness goal these days. If you’ve been hearing the term everywhere like I have, and thinking body recompo-what, you’re not alone.

So, what is body recomp? Whether you knew it or not, chances are, you’ve probably pursued it at some point. If you’ve ever set out to reduce body fat or build muscle, you’ve been working toward a body recomposition goal. When people say body recomp these days, they really mean simultaneously losing fat and building muscle, not just one or the other.

Meet the expert: Brittany Busse, MD, is the chief medical officer and cofounder of ViTel Health.

Unlike simply losing weight, this approach isn’t about the number on the scale; it’s about improving the ratio of fat to muscle in your body for better health, performance, and aesthetics. (Oftentimes, when people talk about wanting to look "toned," they're really talking about body recomp, since you need low amounts of body fat to see the muscle you've built up.)

And, while body recomposition is completely possible, it can be a little more technical than other fitness goals. Here are the core things you need to know to get started on your body recomp journey.

Get started with our exclusive body recomp guide.

First: a quick refresher. Body composition refers to a percentage breakdown of how much body fat, lean mass (that is, muscle!), and bone you've got on your body. Body recomposition is the process through which you change that breakdown.

These are the five most important things to keep in mind when trying to make that happen.

At the most basic level, losing fat requires a calorie deficit; you need to burn more than you consume. Working with a nutritionist or doctor, you can determine exactly what this means for you, but for body recomposition, it's only a slight deficit that you should be shooting for. We’re talking 250 to 500 calories max.

Keep in mind: “Weight loss should not be confused with fat loss,” Brittany Busse, MD, the chief medical officer and cofounder of ViTel Health previously told Women's Health. “Much of weight loss can also be loss of muscle mass.”

And, you don't want to lose muscle mass, particularly if your goal is body recomp. That’s why protein is critical, Dr. Busse says—but it’s just one piece of the puzzle. Tracking all three macros (protein, carbs, and fat) can go a long way in helping you stay full, energized, and strong while pursuing body recomp.

#4851. Morning Minute: Ethereum Focuses on Security As AI Threats Rise

Morning Minute: Ethereum Focuses on Security As AI Threats Rise

Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.

The Ethereum Foundation has doubled its protocol security team and made cryptography its top priority. The reason isn’t quantum computers.

Protocol lead Kev Wedderburn wrote this week that “recently AI emerged as a more urgent risk”, and the distinction matters. The quantum threat has always been a hardware problem, and hardware problems announce themselves years in advance because somebody has to build the machine. The AI version is a math problem. A sufficiently capable model could find a structural shortcut in the elliptic curve cryptography that secures Ethereum and Bitcoin, and it would need no special hardware to do it.

Researcher Justin Drake raised the scenario in October. In a worst case, he said, existing signatures could become vulnerable within months.

An Anthropic mathematician named Levent Alpöge posted a claimed proof of the Riemann hypothesis, produced with an unreleased version of Claude, along with a formalized proof archive. Nobody has verified it. It doesn’t break elliptic curve cryptography and nobody is claiming it does. What it does is demonstrate the capability class Drake was describing, roughly a month after he described it.

Axios reported Tuesday that more than two dozen people familiar with internal discussions at OpenAI and Anthropic say employees worry their most advanced unreleased models may never be safe enough to release. The concerns named include reward hacking, models that hide or misrepresent their reasoning, and systems capable enough to find weaknesses in the safety measures their own developers built. OpenAI’s chief scientist proposed Sunday that labs agree on shared limits on how far they train models.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short ETH with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

The plan replaces elliptic curves with hash-based cryptography, which rests on fewer structural assumptions about mathematics. It touches how users authorize transactions, how validators secure the network, and how layer-2 data gets verified. Drake proposed pulling the deadline from December 2029 to December 2028. Ethlabs withdrew its faster-block-production proposal from the Hegotá upgrade to free up engineers. The Foundation has deployed AI agents to hunt bugs in its own infrastructure, which is a reasonable response and also an admission about where the advantage currently sits.

Wedderburn’s own framing: it’s harder than the Merge, and there’s less time. He also acknowledged that moving faster makes it easier to ship bugs.

Bitcoin is on the same road. Blockstream’s Jonas Nick published a security analysis of SHRINCS last week, the apparent frontrunner to replace Bitcoin’s signatures, with sizes running from 548 bytes to 5,777 against today’s 64 to 71.

So the AI threat is looming (and accelerating), but the two largest crypto assets have teams that are responding. Now we wait on action, and more assurances that crypto is safe from AI threats. Assurances that could ensure the bottom is in fact in, if and when they arrive…

#4850. BlackRock launches tokenized money market fund accepting stablecoins in Hong Kong

The tokenized fund launched with approximately $100 million in assets, with Standard Chartered and Ant International participating as seed investors.

According to a Tuesday report by the South China Morning Post, the BlackRock HKD Digital Liquidity Fund launched with approximately $100 million in assets, with British banking group Standard Chartered and Ant International, a Singapore-based digital payments company spun out of China’s Ant Group, as seed investors.

The launch allows institutional investors to earn returns on their stablecoin holdings by investing directly in the fund, eliminating the need to convert their digital assets into traditional currency before investing.

The Hong Kong dollar, distinct from mainland China’s yuan, has been pegged to the US dollar since 1983.

Related: Hong Kong takes tokenized settlement to 24/7, plans stablecoin trials

BlackRock’s seed investors are also playing broader roles in the fund’s operations and adoption.

Subscriptions and redemptions can be carried out using HKDAP, a Hong Kong dollar-pegged stablecoin issued by Anchorpoint Financial, a joint venture between Standard Chartered, telecommunications company HKT and blockchain investment firm Animoca Brands. Standard Chartered also serves as the fund’s custodian, administrator, trustee and tokenization agent.

For Ant International, integrating the fund would support round-the-clock liquidity management across its global operations. According to the company’s disclosures, its payment services support more than 300 payment methods across 220 markets and process an average of over 20 million transactions daily.

BlackRock’s fund documentation shows that the fund began operations on Nov. 16, investing primarily in short-term securities issued or guaranteed by governments and high-grade bank deposits, with a net seven-day yield of 2.03% as of Tuesday. The fund may also accept tokenized deposits, while retail investors are limited to conventional Hong Kong dollars.

The fund’s launch follows HSBC’s Nov. 19 announcement that retail customers could invest in a tokenized money market fund using its Hong Kong dollar-backed stablecoin, RedCoin (RCHKD). HSBC and Anchorpoint Financial secured Hong Kong’s first two stablecoin issuer licenses in April, eight months after the city’s stablecoin regulatory framework took effect.

#4849. Pottery Barn Jake Leather Sofa Review, Tested by AD (2026)

I’ve wanted a leather sofa for many years, but I could never find a color I liked—a detail just as important to me as the material. I wasn’t interested in the usual black, brown, or cognac options, instead preferring something less traditional but not squarely trendy. And then I discovered Pottery Barn’s Jake Leather Sofa in Vintage Hunter, which hit my sofa sweet spot, exuding a deep confidence that reads as rich, grounded, and classy. Its sophisticated presence anchors my living room without overpowering the space.

If you don’t love the stately green hue as much as I do, that hardly means the Jake isn’t your room’s match. The sofa’s customization options—another major selling point—are robust: In addition to being able to choose from a broad range of leathers and upholstery colors, I could also select the style of the seat and back cushions, adding up to a piece of furniture that feels more personal than an off-the-sales-floor purchase. With its slim arms, low profile, plush cushions, and bronze-finished metal legs, it strikes a balance between streamlined and inviting.

How much does it cost? Are there payment plans available?

The cost of the Jake depends on the size, material, and cushion configuration you choose, falling somewhere between $2,000 and $6,000 for most designs. To save yourself from shopping-cart sticker shock, price out the exact model you want, since the leather grade and sofa width can meaningfully change the total. For instance, my 86-inch-wide, 36-inch-deep model in Vintage Hunter retails for $3,999, but a 70-inch-wide, 36-inch-deep loveseat in a Chocolate Performance fabric costs $3,099, and is sometimes on sale for less.

What are the upholstery or customization options? Did you choose any?

There’s little you can’t choose with the Jake. Available in an extensive selection of leather colors and finishes, you can also pick the number of back cushions you’d like (two or three) and style of seat cushion (two separate or a single bench). For my vintage leather sofa in Hunter, I decided on one bench-style seat cushion and three back cushions.

What is the lead time for customization, manufacturing, and delivery?

It took about six weeks for my sofa to arrive at my home after I ordered it, which felt reasonable for a piece with customized upholstery and cushion selections.

What kind of couch or seating arrangement did you have before, and what drew you to your new couch?

My previous sofa was a smaller turquoise felt sleeper from Mopio that I bought on Amazon; its blue undertones made it feel brighter and more casual. I loved the feel, but dog hair got caught in it easily and was hard to vacuum. This Hunter shade is deeper, moodier, and much closer to the sophisticated design I had envisioned for the room.

What was the delivery process like? What was the assembly process like? How long did it take, and how many people did it require?

Receiving the sofa could not have been easier, thanks to Pottery Barn’s included white-glove delivery service. Two people brought the sofa into my home, placed it where I wanted it, and assembled it on the spot. The entire process took about 10 minutes. For a substantial piece of furniture like this sofa, the luxury delivery experience was a major advantage.

What are the dimensions? How does it fit in your space? Would it be better suited for a certain type of home?

I chose the 85-inch-wide version, which measures 36 inches deep and 32 inches high, and it fits my apartment almost perfectly. It feels generous enough to function as the room’s main seating option without commandeering the full focus of the room. I would recommend this size for a midsize living area, provided that the access points can accommodate its width. As always, measuring the doorway, elevator, stairwell, and turning radius before you click “buy” is just as crucial as measuring the piece’s final spot.

Sit test: Is it comfortable? Does it feel well-made? Does the couch have a tendency to sag?

Comfort is where the Jake has exceeded my expectations. It feels supportive and substantial, and the cushions have held their shape without developing an obvious sag. In the four to five months I’ve had the Jake, several visitors have already stayed over and shared that they’ve experienced restful nights on this couch.

The only recurring quirk I’ve experienced is that the seat cushion occasionally slides forward a smidge. It is easy to nudge back into place and has never become a serious annoyance. It’s also entirely possible that this funky detail has more to do with my sitting tendencies than the sofa’s construction.

Is the sofa suitable for particular decor styles and if so, which?

The Jake naturally fits with modern and contemporary interiors. Its low, linear profile, narrow arms, and metal legs provide a clean architectural quality, while the Hunter leather adds depth and character. However, with the right design elements in place, the sofa would also look at home in decidedly relaxed spaces, with warm woods, woven textiles, vintage pieces, or more traditional accessories.

Is it durable and practical in a modern home?

Despite its sophisticated appearance, this sofa isn’t your grandfather’s precious showpiece that exists for looking at and not sitting on. Rather, I’ve found it to be durable, practical, and comfortable to actually use daily.

But that’s just for humans; pets are the bigger consideration here. I have a dog, and a few scratches have already appeared on the leather. My current remediation system is to cover the sofa with a sheet when we are home and remove it before guests arrive. It works, but anyone hoping for completely carefree pet ownership should be realistic about the care needs of a leather sofa before purchasing this polished piece.

The Jake might fare better with children than with a dog, since typical spills are often easy to address quickly, while claw marks are harder to reverse (if possible to do at all). I am planning to try a leather conditioner to soften the appearance of the scratches, though I have not tested it yet. Before applying any product, I would follow Pottery Barn’s care instructions to spot-test it in an inconspicuous area first. Ultimately, the Jake is probably better suited to a pet-free home, or to any owner willing to go whatever lengths necessary to protect and maintain the leather.

Do the photos do this product justice? Was there anything you were surprised to see IRL?

The sofa looks remarkably similar in person to how it appears online, including the depth of the Hunter color and the overall proportions. There was no unpleasant reveal on delivery day; the sofa I had spent weeks picturing was essentially the sofa that arrived.

Would the couch be easy to move into another room? Would it be easy to move to another apartment or home by yourself?

While it’s more manageable to move than other full-size leather sofas may be, largely in light of its removable legs and loose cushions, I wouldn’t call the Jake a portable sofa. It’s not modular, but rather comes in a single piece, so moving it to another room or home is certainly not a single-person job. However, assuming the doorways and corners cooperate, rehoming its 85-inch span should be possible, so long as you have help on hand.

Comfort: A+Value: ADelivery and assembly: A+Style: A+Overall couch rating: A

#4846. CFTC sets new prediction market rules as more firms seek US entry

The US regulator has approved permanent reporting rules for certain event contracts as more companies look to launch prediction markets.

The US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has approved new reporting rules for prediction markets as more companies look to enter the industry.

Under the new rules, announced on Monday, exchanges will report certain event contracts in a similar way as traditional futures and options trades. They will also no longer need to seek individual no-action relief from the CFTC for these reporting requirements.

The regulator said the rules will replace temporary reporting relief that exchanges have relied on for years. CFTC Chairman Michael Selig described the previous no-action letters as “band-aids for unworkable regulations.”

The new rules help to make it clearer how prediction markets should report their trading activity, especially as more companies look to enter the industry. As of September, the CFTC said in its final rule that it was reviewing at least 12 applications from companies looking to launch exchanges that could offer these types of contracts.

Notably, the rules apply to certain fully collateralized event contracts – meaning sufficient collateral must be set aside to cover any potential losses. New exchange operators will still need regulatory approval to launch.

Related: US Senate advances prediction market restrictions with DEATH BETS Act

According to the CFTC’s final rule, exchanges certified about 1,600 event contracts for listing in 2025, compared with an average of just five new listings per year between 2006 and 2020.

While the CFTC expects the new rules to lower some reporting costs, exchanges will also be required to collect more information about their users, including names, addresses, occupations and employers.

The regulator added that knowing where traders work could help identify those who have access to inside information or could influence the outcome of an event. These concerns have also drawn attention from US lawmakers, who on Friday proposed rewarding whistleblowers with up to 30% of the financial penalties collected in certain prediction market fraud cases.

Exchanges will have one year from the rule’s publication in the Federal Register to meet the customer information requirements. Meanwhile, other changes will take effect in phases, with some deadlines occurring in 2027.

Related: CFTC staff say exchanges can count Bitcoin toward operating reserves

The CFTC is also working on separate rules that could help clarify which events prediction markets can offer contracts on. The White House received the rules for review on Nov. 20, but the final text has not yet been made public.

On Nov. 19, the US Senate also passed the DEATH BETS Act, a bill that would ban federally regulated prediction markets from offering contracts tied to war, military operations, terrorism, assassinations and individual deaths. The bill is still awaiting House approval.

The latest reporting rules also do not resolve the ongoing legal battle between the CFTC and state gambling regulators over who should regulate prediction markets. The CFTC says that event contracts fall under its authority and has sued 12 states that argue sports-related contracts should be subject to state gambling laws.

#4845. Ukraine Passes Law to Legalize and Tax Its Crypto Market From July 2027

Ukraine Passes Law to Legalize and Tax Its Crypto Market From July 2027

Ukraine's parliament has passed a law to legalize the country's crypto market and tax virtual asset transactions, with the new rules set to take effect on July 1, 2027.

The Verkhovna Rada approved bill No. 10225-d in its second reading and as a whole on Wednesday, with 271 lawmakers voting in favor, Yaroslav Zhelezniak, first deputy chair of the parliament's finance, tax and customs committee, said on Telegram. The law still needs to be signed by President Volodymyr Zelensky.

Zhelezniak said the law would bring in an extra 15 billion hryvnias (around $330 million) in budget revenue.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short BTC with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

Under the law, individuals will pay 18% personal income tax and a 5% military levy on profits from crypto transactions, according to state news agency Ukrinform. Swapping one crypto asset for another will not be taxed, and losses from previous years can be carried forward.

For crypto bought before the law takes effect, a reduced rate will apply when holders cash out into traditional currency during 2027 and 2028: 5% plus the military levy. Zhelezniak wrote that the reduced rate would apply to "the entire volume," rather than only to profits.

Oversight will be split between the National Securities and Stock Market Commission and the National Bank of Ukraine (NBU). The central bank will be responsible for stablecoins, and can set its own rules for their use, including allowing or banning their circulation.

The NBU will also authorize and supervise issuers of e-money tokens and providers that exchange virtual assets for traditional money, the central bank said in a statement, according to Interfax-Ukraine.

Ukraine first moved to legalize crypto in 2021, and Zelensky signed a law on virtual assets in March 2022, weeks after Russia's full-scale invasion. Soon after, the NBU banned purchases of crypto with hryvnias.

The new bill, which adds tax rules and aligns Ukraine's regulation more closely with the EU's as part of its bid for membership, passed its first reading in September 2025.

Ukraine has also explored other ways to bring crypto into the state's orbit. Lawmakers submitted a bill to create a strategic crypto reserve in June 2025, and in June 2026, the country placed more than $8.3 million in seized USDT under state management for the first time.

#4843. Can This Supplement Really Fight Inflammation? Here's What Doctors Say.

NAC promises it can improve your health and longevity. That might be a false alarm.

IS THERE ANYTHING NAC can’t do? Well, if you listen to the supplement industry, no, not really.

N-Acetylcysteine, or NAC, in its supplement form, has managed to accumulate a large number of alleged benefits in recent years. Depending on who you listen to, NAC supplements can allegedly boost your immune system, detoxify your body, improve cognitive function, increase energy levels, slow aging, increase fertility, reduce inflammation, prevent respiratory infections, and decrease oxidative stress.

That’s a whole lot of responsibility to place on one single supplement.

Add that to the fact that NAC is a proven medical treatment for a couple of specific diagnoses, and you have the perfect setup. Supplement companies can extrapolate evidence into claims that go way beyond current scientific evidence. That’s been a blessing and a curse for NAC manufacturers—and a legal headache that the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) just made a major move to solve with the proposed creation of a new regulatory category just for NAC.

The legal maneuvering is complicated and, if finalized, would allow NAC to be considered a supplement but still a medical treatment which technically isn’t allowed—yet. Basically, there’s a lot to unpack here.

So what can NAC supplement do? And what even is NAC? Is it safe? Let’s break it all down.

NAC IS A sulfur-containing compound, a precursor of the amino acid L-cysteine. In medicinal or supplement form, NAC is converted directly into cysteine, which is then used to make and deliver glutathione, a powerful antioxidant that the body uses to scavenge free radicals and manage oxidative stress. (Yes, the body is a complex system.)

While NAC isn’t found in food, cysteine is readily available in animal proteins, legumes, dairy, nuts and seeds, and some vegetables. Compared to dietary cysteine, NAC supplements are a faster, more stable way of increasing glutathione levels.

NAC supplements are available in powders, capsules, liquids, and tablets. And while NAC has legitimate medical uses, it’s not officially FDA-approved as a supplement as of this second. Of course, this hasn’t stopped the supplement industry from selling it—or influencers from promoting it.

NAC has been in a weird legal gray area for years. Because it’s an actual medical treatment, it technically can’t be classified as a supplement, even though it’s often presented that way.

The FDA’s proposed rule would classify NAC as the first-ever “Dietary Ingredient Not Excluded from the Dietary Supplement Definition.” Basically, it will be allowed to span the categories of supplement and medication, which has never been done before. If finalized, this ruling would “provide for the lawful use of certain ingredients in dietary supplements that would otherwise be excluded from the dietary supplement definition,” per an FDA constituent update.

The proposed rule would allow products that contain NAC to be lawfully marketed as dietary supplements, as long as they’re not otherwise in violation of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act). In theory, this may eventually apply to other supplement-ish ingredients; Right now, this is centered around NAC.

The proposed rule is open for public comment for 60 days. It’s not clear when the FDA when issue a final rule.

This won’t really impact the general public if it’s finalized. Instead, it clears up potential legal issues surrounding NAC. “This will more formally allow sales of NAC over the counter, without a prescription,” says Jamie Alan, PharmD, PhD, a professor of pharmacology and toxicology at Michigan State University in East Lansing.

While some members of the MAHA movement have pushed for this, Alan says it’s also a case of “well, why not.” She explains, “It is generally safe, and I agree with that assessment. It is also being sold as a supplement already so, why not?”

Alan stresses that this move doesn’t suddenly legitimize all NAC supplements or claims surrounding them. “If you are buying a supplement, you aren’t necessarily guaranteed that the bottle contains what it says it does,” she says. “There really isn’t evidence yet in my opinion that supplementing with NAC as a dietary supplement will be life-changing for the vast majority of people.”

NAC is the standard treatment for acetaminophen (Tylenol) overdose. High levels of acetaminophen deplete the liver of glutathione, which is required for the body’s detox pathways. If you’re curious about the geeky scientific mechanism: Quickly repleting glutathione by way of an intravenous NAC infusion helps clear the excess metabolites from the overdose and prevent liver damage.

NAC is also a mucolytic, meaning it can break down thick mucus in the respiratory system. (Yum.) While recent research found that NAC may help with with COPD and chronic bronchitis feel less worse, more investigation is needed to clearly establish effects and benefits.

WELL, NOT ALL that much. Other scientific trials have looked at NAC’s effects on conditions including mood and compulsive disorders, Alzheimer’s, Schizophrenia, and chronic pain. Overall, results have been mixed and largely unremarkable. For most of these conditions and disorders, larger-scale clinical trials are still needed.

So while it’s true that research does exist on NAC and wider health benefits, most of the new research trials examining NAC’s effects use doses that are far higher than what the average person would take, and in forms that are not available to the public.

This hasn’t stopped wellness influencers from broadcasting that NAC supplements can help heal whatever ails you.

Many of these influencers argue that because glutathione may reduce oxidative stress, NAC is amazing for longevity and anti-aging. It’s simple, they argue: Because oxidative stress is associated with aging, increasing glutathione with NAC supplements slows biological aging.

Except raising levels of glutathione in the body does not necessarily translate into a desired outcome. Science agrees: There is no long-term human evidence that showing that this suppresses oxidative stress to the level of having a clinically meaningful outcome. Taking NAC for “healthy aging” is more marketing than anything else at this point.

FOR MOST HEALTHY people, NAC supplements appear to be safe in doses between 600 milligrams (mg) to 1800mg per day. However, doses on the higher end of that range may have a higher risk of side effects such as gastrointestinal upset.

NAC is not recommended for people with clotting disorders. There are also some potential drug interactions between NAC and immunosuppressants, so it’s always a good idea to get a doctor or pharmacist to cross-reference any supplements with the medications you’re taking.

Again, remember that the supplement industry is largely unregulated. Always buy from reputable companies, and look for products that are third-party tested to ensure that what’s on the label is actually what’s in the bottle.

NAC has some legitimate—and even life-saving—medical uses, and research is constantly evolving. But what the supplements don’t have at this point, is compelling human evidence showing that NAC has any clinically meaningful effects in healthy people.

Abby Langer, RD is the owner of Abby Langer Nutrition, a Toronto-based nutrition consulting and communications company

#4842. Coldcard reveals how Bitcoin wallet flaw went undetected for over 5 years

Coldcard maker Coinkite explained why years of security checks failed to catch the flaw and said it has yet to decide on compensation for affected customers.

Bitcoin hardware wallet maker Coinkite has detailed how a security flaw in its Coldcard devices went undetected for more than five years despite several independent security reviews, including those using artificial intelligence (AI).

In a Nov. 23 postmortem report, Coinkite said that while its security checks confirmed the wallets had the correct system for generating secure recovery phrases, the company never verified whether the wallets were actually using it. As a result, a software error caused the wallets to use a weaker system instead, making the recovery phrases easier for hackers to guess.

A Bitcoin hardware wallet is a physical device that stores private keys offline, while a recovery phrase is a series of words that allows users to restore access to their funds if the device is lost or damaged.

Coinkite said at least 15 independent security reviews and research efforts failed to catch the flaw before the thefts began. It added that the weaker system went undetected because the recovery phrases looked normal and could still pass some security tests.

The flaw allowed hackers to steal at least 1,789 Bitcoin (BTC), worth around $114.7 million at the time of the thefts, Galaxy Research reported in August. Coinkite said it fixed the flaw on July 31 and introduced further security measures in August.

The report says that as of Nov. 18, Coinkite had received around 300 loss-related support tickets associated with 242 accounts. The company also said that the actual number of victims was likely higher and that it is still exploring ways to help affected customers but has yet to decide on a compensation plan.

Coinkite said it still does not know who stole the funds or how the hackers found the flaw. The company said law enforcement authorities are also investigating the thefts, and the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security has opened a separate case.

The company continues to urge affected users to update their software, create new recovery phrases and move their funds to new wallets, warning that software updates cannot make previously affected recovery phrases safe.

Cointelegraph contacted Coinkite for comment on its compensation plans but had not received a response by publication.
